questions.stem: How does DataOps relate to DevOps and DevSecOps?
options: It replaces them for data projects
It is unrelated and follows Waterfall principles
It removes CI/CD from the process
It follows the same principles but adds elements related to the data domain
It applies only to machine learning models
questions.explanation: DataOps follows the same principles as DevOps and DevSecOps, with a few additional elements specific to the data domain.

questions.stem: What does DataOps make sure of with respect to data?
options: That data is stored only in a data warehouse
That data is properly integrated with source and target, flows through automated best-practice pipelines, is highly secured and is of high quality
That data is deleted after each sprint
That data is used only by data scientists
That data is held in a single file format
questions.explanation: DataOps focuses on the data-related aspects of operations: integration with source and target, automated pipelines, security and quality.

questions.stem: DevOps does not care whether a project is a data project or a mobile application project. What does DataOps focus on instead?
options: Where the data is coming from and going to, why it is coming, how it will be used, how much it cost and how much it will monetise
Which programming language the application uses
How many servers the application needs
Which team owns the mobile application
How quickly the user interface loads
questions.explanation: DataOps is concerned with the data itself: its origin and destination, its purpose and usage, its cost and its monetisation.

questions.stem: Which step appears at the start of the DataOps process flow but not in the DevOps flow of Development, Build, Testing, Deployment and Run?
questions.explanation: The DataOps process flow begins with Regular Integration before Development, Build, Testing, Deployment, Delivery/Run and Monitoring and Feedback.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a key element of DataOps?
questions.explanation: The key elements are ETL/ELT, Agile and CI/CD, Component Design, Environment Management, Governance Security and Change Control, Automated Testing, and Collaboration and Self-Service.

questions.stem: What is described as the practice for implementing DataOps?
options: Implement DataOps under the umbrella of DevOps, including CI/CD
Implement DataOps as a standalone process outside DevOps
Implement DataOps only after MLOps is in place
Implement DataOps only for structured data
questions.explanation: The stated practice is to implement DataOps under the umbrella of DevOps, including CI/CD.

questions.stem: Which key element of DataOps is specifically concerned with moving and transforming data between systems?
questions.explanation: ETL or ELT is the DataOps element that covers extracting, transforming and loading data between source and target.

questions.stem: What is the final step in the DataOps process flow?
questions.explanation: The DataOps flow ends with Regular Monitoring and Feedback, a step added beyond the DevOps flow.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the questions DataOps asks about data?
options: Which mobile platform the application targets
How much the data cost and how much it will monetise
Which cloud vendor has the cheapest compute
How many developers are on the team
Which version control system is used
questions.explanation: DataOps asks where data comes from and goes, why, how it will be used, and how much it cost and how much it will monetise.

questions.stem: Which two qualities does DataOps ensure the data has as it flows through pipelines?
questions.explanation: DataOps makes sure the data flowing in is highly secured and of high quality.
